newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -Prices end down at least 1/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -Prices end down at least 1/8.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices ended a quiet session down at least 1/8 point amid steeper U.S. Treasury bond losses, as players looked toward Tuesday's $626 million New York City deal.
"I'm sure we're softer, but where (prices are) I couldn't really tell you because I just didn't see all that much activity," one trader said. "There's a lot of bonds out there too."
The trader added that given recent stock market volatility, a lot of brokers' attention has been focused there.

"And when the stock market starts getting a little shaky like today...I think it starts to make them and their customers nervous," he said. "Basically they are less focused on bond type of stuff when they are trying to hold customers hands."
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 36.52 points.
A municipal analyst said high-grade issues weakened by two basis points, while dollar bonds declined by 1/4 point. A second trader judged the overall market down 1/8 point.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed down 21/32 at 98-11/32 yield 6.63 percent. In debt futures, the March municipal contract was 9/32 at 115-9/32. The March T-bond contract closed down 16/32 at 112-16/32. The MOB spread was 81 ticks.

Earlier Monday, the Federal Reserve board reported that U.S. industrial production rose 0.9 percent in November against a 0.2 percent drop in October. Economists polled by Reuters had expected a 0.6 percent gain. Capacity utilization was also above expectations at 83.3 percent in November, up from 82.9 in October.

As for new issues, New York City received $158 million of retail orders for its $626 million offering, a city official said. The deal, via Lehman Brothers, is one of 12 negotiated issues totaling $1.298 billion scheduled for Tuesday.
"I'll take a peak at it," Tom Moles, a managing director at J&W Seligman said, adding that he was unsure whether he would be a buyer. "I've kind of pulled in my horns until the end of the year."
Other deals include a $224 million Indiana Health Facility Financing Authority offering via Smith Barney Inc and a $189 million University of Minnesota Regents deal through Goldman Sachs & Co.
Competitive sales are expected to number 28 and total $258 million. The biggest scheduled deal is an $87 million Los Angeles Municipal Improvement Corporation deal set for noon (EST).
